description: CalWeedMapper is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by California Invasive Plant Council; Calflora; Consortium of California Herbaria. CalWeedMapper gives natural resource managers and others a way to generate maps and reports of invasive plant distribution in California. Information from the site can help decision makers identify management opportunities at various scales. Users can view current ranges of a variety of invasive plants, and projected suitable range for the same plants in 2050. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
